label: VERIFIED
extraction: Anthropic blog on five multi-agent coordination patterns: 1) Generator-verifier for quality-critical output with explicit evaluation criteria, 2) Orchestrator-subagent for clear task decomposition with bounded subtasks (Claude Code uses this), 3) Agent teams for parallel, independent, long-running subtasks, 4) Agent swarms for fluid handoffs between agents, 5) Capability-based systems for routing to specialized agents. Generator-verifier is simplest and most deployed - generator produces output, verifier evaluates against criteria. Orchestrator-subagent: lead agent plans, delegates, synthesizes; subagents handle specific responsibilities. Agent teams: multiple agents work in parallel on independent subtasks with communication. Key insight: multi-agent architectures provide value when addressing specific constraints single agent cannot overcome (context overflow, parallel work need, specialization). Decision framework: reserve multi-agent for cases with clear benefits justifying additional cost. Coordination patterns compose rather than compete.
